q-132982.solution:
Let $u=@@u@@.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=@@v@@\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=t\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can solve the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-16t}{@@u@@}\,\text{d}t & =-16\int \frac{1}{@@u@@}\cdot t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-16\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+K \\  & =-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(@@u@@)+K\end{aligned}
$$

q-12501.problem: Calculate the integral of $\frac{{x}^{2}}{@@u@@}$ with respect to $x.$
q-12501.solution:
Let $u=@@u@@.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=@@v@@\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

and we can solve the resulting integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{@@u@@}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{@@u@@}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|@@u@@|+C\end{aligned}
$$
